why: Issue #226: 'only sections with relevant controls should render'. Accessibility shipped declared and EMPTY, which is where the rule came from; issue #289's motion toggle filled it, so every declared section has a control today and the rule is measured on a section emptied at runtime instead -- a control hidden by `display: none`, which is what a `--hidden` class resolves to and what #227's capability hiding will do. Without the rule that section opens as a heading over nothing, the 'permanently disabled settings players have to decode' the UI direction rules out.
killedBy: hud: the Settings sections (issue #226) collapses a section whose last control is hidden, and brings it back -- the rule reads the DOM, not a list
